text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-Heated discussions extended till today the meeting of the five-nation ceasefire monitoring committee in Naqoura, south Lebanon, which started discussing on Monday four complaints filed by Lebanon and Israel.
-Military appeals court ordered the release on bail of Lebanese journalist Pierre Atallah, charged with contacts with Israel. The court set bail at six million pounds.
-The January 2 weekly treasury bill issue raised 307.5 billion pounds.
-Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu received General Lahd, leader of the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army and said "protecting the interests of our allies is a pre-condition for any peace settlement".
-Palestinian refugee camps went on one day strike on Monday to protest the social policy of the United Nations Relief and Welfare Agency (UNRWA).
-Byblos Bank, which issued a $50 million Eurobond in September, said it plans a new issue this year for at least that amount.

-Magistrate demanded the death penalty for 13 alleged members of the radical Islamist group Esbat al-Ansar after charging them with trying to assassinate two Moslem religious leaders and undertake acts of sabotage.
-Damascus expects Israeli military action in Syria and Lebanon, Syrian newspapers said.
Prime minister Hariri will pay a quick visit to Damascus to discuss the recent developments in south Lebanon.
